key_insight: AtomWorld-Mirror replaces slow event-by-event atomistic replay with a time-aware macro-step world model that predicts physically reachable structural changes and elapsed time for long-horizon materials evolution.
engineering_relevance: This could accelerate atomistic studies of diffusion, defect growth, interfacial reactions, and fracture by preserving structural validity while reducing simulation cost by orders of magnitude.
method: Distills short micro-event segments into latent macro-step dynamics between key states.
Predicts sparse structural edits plus accumulated physical time in a jointly constrained framework.
Uses local reachability, inventory conservation, and continuous-time consistency to keep transitions physically plausible.
evidence_signal: Across five atomic systems, including Cu-rich RPV steel, Cu-Zr metallic glass, and Li3N-based solid electrolyte cases, the method reports 10^3–10^4× speedups over event-by-event simulation.
watch_item: Macro-step inference may depend on the quality and coverage of training trajectories, so unseen failure modes or rare transitions could be harder to capture reliably.
paper_title: AtomWorld-Mirror: Macro-Step World Modeling of Critical Evolution Backbones for Materials Dynamics
